sources_considered.why: Primary confirmation of operational launch and expansion after the post.
Primary description of an additional deployed generative search experience, including contrary early traffic observations.
Independent browsing measurements bear on how generated summaries mediate access to external websites.
A later primary research report measures international expansion and source-selection differences, but remains focused on search.

evidence_items.explanation: Google confirms that generated search overviews had launched and expanded after the post. This establishes operational reliance for this feature; the company's assessment of positive feedback is not treated as independent outcome evidence.

evidence_items.locator: Description of the generative search experience
evidence_items.explanation: The announcement describes a generative experience already serving a small share of queries, adding evidence of operational adoption. Microsoft also reports that early click totals were maintained, which limits any assumption that such adoption necessarily reduces external traffic.

evidence_items.locator: Results comparing traditional-link clicks with and without AI summaries
evidence_items.explanation: The browsing study associates AI summaries with fewer external-result clicks. It covers Google and does not randomly assign summaries; searches were reconstructed in April, so it cannot independently establish a web-wide causal increase in automated control.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Sinan Aral, Haiwen Li and Rui Zuo
evidence_items.explanation: The study reports international expansion of AI search and differences in the information sources it presents. Its search-specific measurements strengthen evidence of a trend but do not settle the broader claim about dependence across the web.

unresolved_gaps: No representative measure establishes increased automated control across the web and attributes it to expanding generative AI reliance.
The evidence establishes operational use, not indispensability.
No dated event meets the early-resolution rule.
